Why Top Right?

Different customer barriers call for different messages. Gemini analyzes and drafts; Zapier handles eligibility and execution; the CRM Manager judges campaign suitability before any email is sent.

If AI only brainstormed options while the manager independently ran the campaign, the task would lean toward Bottom Right. Placement remains a reasoned interpretation, not a measured fact.

06 / THREE TAKEAWAYS

What the experiment taught us.

01 / HUMAN DESIGNS

People set the guardrails.

I defined the campaign objective, wrote Gemini instructions and set decision boundaries. AI generated options and email drafts within that design.

02 / HUMAN VERIFIES

Correct AI ≠ safe execution.

I caught a workflow-control error: Gemini said NO_CAMPAIGN, but Zapier still requested approval. I added a Filter and retested.

03 / HUMAN JUDGES

Approval governs the action.

The CRM Manager checks relevance, accuracy and risk. Approve releases Gmail; Reject stops it. A production agent also needs independent data checks.

CORE REFLECTION

Humans design the agent, validate its logic and judge customer-facing decisions. AI handles repeatable analysis and drafting; automation only executes when the decision gate permits it.

Agent card · job, trigger, tools, boundaries, human check

Agent name

AI-Powered Banking CRM Onboarding Agent. Built and tested on 18 October 2026; approximately 4 hours, S$0 direct monetary cost on Zapier trial.

1 · Job

Analyze synthetic digital-banking onboarding behaviours and prepare relevant first-deposit campaign emails, subject to manager approval before execution.

2 · Trigger

Google Sheets: New Spreadsheet Row, containing a synthetic case ID and customer onboarding status.

3 · Tools

Google Sheets (trigger) → Google AI Studio/Gemini (analysis, three campaign options, recommendation, draft) → Code by Zapier (parse JSON) → Filter by Zapier (campaign eligibility) → Human in the Loop (managerial approval or rejection) → Gmail (send to test inbox).

4 · Must never

Send an email without approval, or knowingly send a first-deposit activation campaign to an already-funded customer. The prototype filters Gemini-generated campaign_status values; it does not independently verify bank transaction data.

5 · Where a person checks

The CRM Manager reviews customer relevance, proposed campaign, reasoning, the specific subject and body, and unsupported claims before Gmail executes an approved communication. Rejected and timed-out approvals prevent the Gmail step.

Q1 analysis · the two map questions, human role and group view

Chosen quadrant — Top Right: “Agents run it, a person judges”

The customer onboarding agent operates an event-driven workflow rather than functioning as an optional brainstorming chatbot. The manager exercises judgement at a decision checkpoint; the workflow implements the approved action.

Question 1 · Is there a single right answer?

No. A customer who browsed deposit instructions might need guidance, while a customer whose attempt failed due to a technical error might need support. A reminder, education or support campaign may be plausible; the best option depends on context, compliance, costs, communications policy and risk. The prototype does not prove which campaign is most effective.

Question 2 · Must humans and AI work together?

For this designed process, yes. Gemini analyzes the supplied behaviour and drafts alternatives and the email. A human manager must assess suitability and decide whether a communication should be executed. The required collaboration is a workflow-design and governance decision, not a claim that a manager literally cannot draft an email alone.

Human checkpoint — who, what, when

Who: CRM Manager. What: customer-context fit, accuracy of any claims, campaign rationale, business risk, exact email text. When: after the Filter passes an eligible draft and before the Gmail action. Approve releases execution; Reject stops the action.

What would move this activity?

If the person queried AI for suggestions and then independently ran the campaign, it would lean toward Bottom Right: “A person decides, AI alongside.” If the task were constrained to deterministic eligibility checks and approved templates and the agent could execute with only periodic audit, it could move toward Bottom Left: “AI alone, with checks.” More automation steps alone do not establish quadrant fit.

Group view

The group agreed on Top Right for the submitted Banking CRM agent. The distinction between Top Right and Bottom Right remained a useful discussion point: recommendation-only assistance is weaker evidence of agent-operated work than a full process with an embedded approval decision. The group map is preserved above.

The right-hand quadrants concern work without a single objectively correct answer. Our Top Right placement is defensible on the workflow evidence, while recognizing that other task definitions may lead to different placement.

Collaboration log · delegation, verification, AI issue, time and cost
DimensionRecord
Delegation to AICustomer behaviour analysis, potential barriers, three intervention options, recommendation and personalized email draft.
AutomationRead sheet rows; parse Gemini JSON; filter eligibility; send approval request; invoke Gmail only after approval.
Human verificationCompared outputs with synthetic input, checked customer relevance, reviewed recommendation and wording, exercised approve/reject branches and checked received emails.
AI content riskAn early AI-generated draft or option referenced unsupported security assurance/certification information. The prompt was constrained against unsupported facts and human review retained; this does not prove all unsupported claims were eliminated.
Workflow errorGemini's correct NO_CAMPAIGN output was not enforced before approval. A Filter was then added and tests repeated.
External errorA separate Gemini service request returned a temporary high-demand error.
Time spentApproximately 4 hours including build, tests, review and fixes.
Direct costS$0 during free trial / test service usage; no claim about production cost.
Three-sentence reflection · exact submission wording
  1. Where it fitted: The agent turned different synthetic customer behaviours into relevant onboarding recommendations and personalized email drafts while retaining managerial approval before execution.
  2. Where it failed: An already-funded customer still reached human approval despite Gemini returning NO_CAMPAIGN, revealing a workflow-control failure; an earlier draft also referenced unverified security information.
  3. What I would change: For production use, I would verify eligibility against authoritative banking data, constrain messaging to approved sources and test campaign effectiveness through controlled experiments.
Evidence archive · screenshots, versions and limitations

Image evidence

Screenshots include the final six-step run, Zapier email notification, CRM Manager approval screen, synthetic sheet, two behaviour-specific emails plus a separate generic test message, historical rejected/filtered runs, and the before-fix NO_CAMPAIGN output and approval request.

Version discipline

Approved → Gmail sent is shown in the final six-step screenshot. Rejected and filtered screenshots come from earlier workflows and are labeled accordingly. A historical filtered screenshot alone is not proof of the same run in final v6.

Privacy and safety

Synthetic customer test cases only. Approver display name is blurred for public sharing. No raw Zap History JSON, email account address or API credentials are embedded. Historical screenshots and statuses are not composites of different runs represented as a single run.

Scope of evidence

This is a prototype test of orchestration and human oversight. It does not establish real conversion uplift, safe live-bank deployment, compliance certification or error-free autonomous operation.

*The number “18 runs” in the hero reflects the count visible in the provided Zap History screenshot on 18 October 2026, including historical, filtered and failed runs; it is not a count of successful end-to-end executions.
